questions.q: What does the balancing segment qualifier make General Ledger do automatically?
options: Balance journal lines so that each value of that segment nets to zero
Convert every journal to the ledger currency
Classify each account as an asset or liability
Restrict which users can see the journal
questions.explain: The balancing segment (commonly company/entity) is automatically balanced by General Ledger so entity-level balance sheets are possible.

questions.q: What does the natural account segment qualifier do?
options: Identifies intercompany transactions
Classifies a value as asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense
Controls which ledger a journal posts to
Restricts data access by business unit
questions.explain: The natural account segment drives financial statement classification — asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense.

questions.q: How do a legal entity, a business unit, and a ledger relate to each other?
options: They are three interchangeable names for the same object
A ledger always equals exactly one business unit and nothing more
A legal entity is a real registered entity; a business unit is an operational grouping reporting to a ledger; a ledger holds the chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and method
A business unit can contain multiple ledgers
questions.explain: Legal entity (registered entity), business unit (operational grouping reporting to a ledger), and ledger (COA/calendar/currency/method) are distinct, related concepts.

questions.q: What does a data access set control?
options: Which journal sources exist in a ledger
Which currencies a ledger supports
Which approval workflow a journal routes through
Which ledgers (and optionally which balancing segment values) a user can access
questions.explain: A data access set governs ledger-level and, optionally, balancing-segment-level access for a user.

questions.q: In Solara Fixtures' four-segment chart of accounts, which segment has no special qualifier of its own?
options: Company
Cost Center
Account
Intercompany
questions.explain: Cost Center is a plain segment used for departmental analysis; it carries no special qualifier, unlike Company (balancing), Account (natural account), and Intercompany.
